subject: Azure Marketplace connector: exemption + integration checklist
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@cloudmart.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BlueOak connector needs billing-hook exemption for Azure listing

Hi Naomi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. BlueOak is excited to list their integration through the Azure Marketplace but the marketplace requires a billing-handshake that conflicts with BlueOak's privacy model. They asked if Redwood can support an exemption path (no direct marketplace billing hooks; our connector would surface a checkout link that routes back to BlueOak) and also if we can provide a short integration checklist for the Azure listing.

Victor (cc'd) is the BlueOak engineering lead and can share their compliance notes. Can Redwood confirm whether we can do an exemption and what product/contracting steps are required? Timebox: they want to be listed in Q4.

Attaching BlueOak's integration notes.

Thanks,
Lena
CloudMart Partnerships

Attachments: blueoak-integration-notes.pdf

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: avery_johnson@redwood.com, Victor Chen <victor@blueoak.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena@cloudmart.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: BlueOak connector needs billing-hook exemption for Azure listing

Marissa / Marcus — forwarding the ask from CloudMart / BlueOak. TL;DR: BlueOak cannot accept Azure's native billing handshake and wants us to be able to ship a connector that presents an external checkout flow (link back to BlueOak) while still being listed in Azure. They need:

- A short product integration checklist we can give to Azure and BlueOak.
- Confirmation on whether Redwood will accept a marketplace listing that routes billing out (i.e., we remain the technical connector but not the billing owner).
- Contracting implications: do we need an exemption clause or amended DPA/SaaS terms? (Avery, please advise).
- Timeline to support the exemption in our deployment model and any gating by Dedicated or Private.

Victor, can you confirm BlueOak's compliance constraints (PCI scope, data residency) in a single-paragraph reply?

Proposed next steps: Marcus to scope product changes and checklist by EOD 9/8; Marissa to coordinate with Azure PM. Avery to draft a short template exemption addendum.

Naomi
Sr. Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment forwarded: blueoak-integration-notes.pdf

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: avery_johnson@redwood.com, Victor Chen <victor@blueoak.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena@cloudmart.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueOak connector needs billing-hook exemption for Azure listing

Thanks Naomi — scoped this with infra and runtime. Key product notes:

- Feasibility: we can support a listing that defers billing to BlueOak by 2 modes: (A) Listing-only metadata + external purchase URL surfaced in the marketplace tile; (B) Full connector but with a redirect to BlueOak checkout during provisioning. Both are implementable without changing core runtime.

- Platform changes: small UI surface for "external purchase URL" and a provisioning flag to skip marketplace billing handlers; backend will need a toggle during provisioning to 1) disable auto-provisioned subscriptions and 2) avoid sending billing webhooks to Azure. Estimated effort: 3 dev-weeks + 1 QA week.

- Gating: Dedicated customers are unaffected. For Hosted customers listed via marketplace, we'll need a policy decision on whether we act as a referral vs. reseller in marketplace records. That is a contractual + marketplace policy item.

- Risk: without marketplace billing hooks we need a clear audit trail for subscription activation (HubSpot + provisioning logs). Adding a short log export would mitigate audit concerns.

Proposed schedule if we start next week: scope doc and integration checklist by 9/10, config toggle and UI by 9/24, testing and docs by 10/8. This aligns with Q4 list target but depends on contract path.

I'll attach a quick connector-impact-matrix to capture edge cases.

Marcus
Product Manager, Integrations

Attachments: connector-impact-matrix.xlsx

From: avery_johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Victor Chen <victor@blueoak.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena@cloudmart.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueOak connector needs billing-hook exemption for Azure listing

Quick legal checklist / next steps from my side:

- Exemption addendum: Drafted a short addendum that makes Redwood a technology provider for listing purposes only and confirms BlueOak retains billing responsibility. This will require: (1) a clause clarifying liability for billing disputes, (2) data processing boundary language (we must not persist BlueOak billing PII), and (3) a representation that BlueOak will meet marketplace commerce requirements.

- Marketplace policy: Azure typically requires a reseller/marketplace owner to accept certain commerce obligations. We should surface the addendum and ask Azure PM whether an "external billing flow" is allowable; Marissa, please escalate this ask in the Azure channel.

- Evidence pack: BlueOak to provide the minimal security/compliance artifacts (they shared a summary PDF) — we need SOC2 scope confirmation before listing. I uploaded a security-evidence-summary.pdf to the shared drive.

- Timeline: Legal target to produce a redlineable doc by 9/13 if we have BlueOak's SOC2 scope and a confirmation from Azure that external billing is permitted.

I'll attach the draft exemption for internal review. If we decide to proceed, Marcus' timeline looks reasonable.

Avery Johnson
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: legal-exemption-draft.docx
